variations.name: Single-building ground-source heat pump equipment
variations.description: Closed- or open-loop borefields paired with electric heat pumps deliver 300-500%-efficient heating and cooling from stable ground temperatures for individual homes and buildings — the workhorse hardware of building geothermal.

companies.name: WaterFurnace International
companies.what: Leading North American residential/commercial geothermal heat pump manufacturer (NIBE-owned) selling variable-speed units through a large dealer network.
companies.signal: Estimated 10-15% share of the geothermal heat pump market; anchor supplier for US residential geothermal.

companies.name: ClimateMaster
companies.what: Oklahoma-based maker of water-source/geothermal heat pumps (Tranquility/TT series) for residential and commercial buildings, part of NIBE's Climate Control Group.
companies.signal: TT series regarded as top-tier on price/efficiency; long-integrated into NIBE's North American geothermal portfolio.

companies.name: NIBE Industrier
companies.what: Swedish heating group that is Europe's largest ground-source heat pump maker and the sector's consolidator (owns WaterFurnace, ClimateMaster/Climate Control Group, CTC and others).
companies.signal: Built the #1 European and North American geothermal positions via serial acquisitions; recovering from the 2023-24 European heat pump destocking slump.

companies.name: Bosch Home Comfort
companies.what: Supplies geothermal and water-source heat pumps (Florida Heat Pump lineage) and is expanding US heat pump manufacturing capacity.
companies.signal: Among the top global GSHP players; investing in US production as IRA tax credits lift demand.

companies.name: Viessmann Climate Solutions
companies.what: German maker of ground-source and air-source heat pumps for European homes and light commercial buildings.
companies.signal: Acquired by Carrier Global for ~€12B (closed January 2024); continues operating as Carrier's European heat pump arm.

companies.name: Stiebel Eltron
companies.what: German family-owned maker of ground-source and air-source heat pumps and electric water heating.
companies.signal: Top-10 global ground-source heat pump manufacturer with major German production expansion.

variations.name: Residential geothermal developers & drilling cost reduction
variations.description: Vertically integrated installers attack the biggest residential geothermal cost — drilling — with purpose-built rigs, software and homebuilder partnerships to make home ground-source systems price-competitive with gas furnaces and air-source heat pumps.

companies.name: Dandelion Energy
companies.what: Google X spinout doing vertically integrated home geothermal; pivoted from one-off retrofits to volume new-construction deployments with production homebuilders.
companies.signal: $40M Series C (2024) after $70M round co-led by Lennar's LenX; deploying geothermal in 1,500+ new Lennar homes in Colorado starting 2025 — one of the largest US residential geothermal deployments ever.

variations.white_space: Retrofit drilling economics remain brutal — rig mobilization and per-foot costs dwarf the heat pump itself, which pushed even category leader Dandelion from one-off retrofits to new-build subdivisions where rigs amortize across adjacent lots. Openings: compact low-cost residential rigs and one-day installs, and replicating the Lennar playbook with other production builders in states with stacked geothermal incentives (CO, NY, MA) — almost no other venture-backed residential geothermal developer exists in the US.

variations.name: Advanced boreholes & commercial-scale geo-exchange
variations.description: Startups apply oilfield drilling automation, groundwater heat exchange and subsurface digital modeling to cut borehole cost and footprint so offices, campuses, high-rises and data centers can replace chillers and boilers with geo-exchange.

companies.name: Bedrock Energy
companies.what: Autonomous, sensor-guided drilling to 1,000+ ft depths enables geothermal HVAC under space-constrained urban sites and data centers, with guaranteed long-term thermal performance.
companies.signal: $12M Series A (Jan 2025) led by Titanium Ventures; first installations in Austin TX and Utah; claims up to 5x faster borehole construction.

companies.name: Celsius Energy (SLB)
companies.what: SLB (Schlumberger) venture using inclined 'compact borehole' star arrays plus digital monitoring to retrofit geo-exchange onto buildings with minimal land.
companies.signal: BNEF Pioneer award; first UK installation 2024; technology deployed in Eversource's Framingham networked geothermal pilot; scaling across France, UK and US.

companies.name: Darcy Solutions
companies.what: University of Minnesota spinout that taps flowing groundwater in aquifers as the heat-exchange medium, extracting roughly an order of magnitude more capacity per borehole than closed loops.
companies.signal: Nearly $5M in competitive DOE/NSF/USDA awards; commercial systems operating across the Upper Midwest.

companies.name: Brightcore Energy
companies.what: Turnkey commercial geothermal and clean-energy developer for the US Northeast, handling design, drilling and financing.
companies.signal: Delivered the 320-borehole heat exchanger for Lendlease's 1 Java Street in Brooklyn — New York State's largest residential geothermal project.

companies.name: Geosource Energy
companies.what: Canadian specialty drilling contractor that builds geo-exchange borefields for high-rise and institutional buildings.
companies.signal: Drilled and looped 1 Java Street's 320 boreholes (each 499 ft); two decades of multi-residential geothermal across Ontario.

variations.name: Networked geothermal & utility thermal energy networks (TENs)
variations.description: Shared borefields and ambient-temperature street loops connect whole neighborhoods to heat pumps, letting gas utilities redeploy pipe-laying crews and rate-based capital into low-carbon heating — enabled by thermal-energy-network legislation now passed in 10+ US states.

companies.name: Eversource
companies.what: Built and operates the first US utility-owned networked geothermal system in Framingham, MA (36 buildings, ~135 customers).
companies.signal: ~$15M pilot in service since June 2024; DOE awarded $8.6M (Dec 2025) with HEET and the City of Framingham to expand into the adjacent neighborhood.

companies.name: National Grid
companies.what: Gas utility developing networked geothermal pilots in Lowell, MA (with UMass Lowell) and at Boston Housing Authority's Franklin Field apartments in Dorchester.
companies.signal: Two Massachusetts pilots advancing under the DPU's new networked-geothermal guidelines.

companies.name: Con Edison
companies.what: Advancing utility thermal energy network pilots in NYC and Westchester, including a Chelsea loop moving data-center/office waste heat to NYCHA housing, Rockefeller Center waste-heat sharing, and a Mount Vernon shared borefield.
companies.signal: Nine New York utility TEN pilots advanced to design under the 2022 UTENJA law; construction phase starting from 2025.

companies.name: HEET
companies.what: Nonprofit incubator that invented the gas-utility 'GeoMicroDistrict' model and brokered the Framingham utility/community pilot; now spreading the playbook nationally.
companies.signal: Co-recipient of the $8.6M DOE Framingham expansion award (Dec 2025); model adopted in legislation across 10+ states.

companies.name: Kensa Group
companies.what: UK's largest ground-source heat pump maker; deploys 'shared ground array' street-by-street networks with in-home shoebox heat pumps — a private-capital version of networked geothermal.
companies.signal: £70M investment from Octopus Energy and Legal & General (2023); UK's first investor-funded GSHP network for 100+ new homes in South Wales (2025); targeting 50,000 pumps/year by 2030.

variations.white_space: Utility pilots depend on rate-based cost recovery and enabling legislation, and almost no independent thermal-energy-network developer-operators exist in the US yet — an opening for ESCO-style companies that design, build and operate networks for utilities, campuses and municipalities as the multi-state legislative wave (MA, NY, CO, WA, MN and others) creates structural demand.

variations.name: District heating development & modernization (4th/5th-generation networks and components)
variations.description: Utilities are converting legacy fossil-fired steam and high-temperature networks to low-temperature 4th/5th-generation systems fed by heat pumps, waste heat and storage, supported by an incumbent supply chain of pre-insulated pipes, substations and smart meters.

companies.name: Vattenfall
companies.what: Operates major district heating networks (Berlin, Amsterdam, Uppsala) plus UK heat ventures, and is publishing the 4G/5G playbook for low-temperature conversion.
companies.signal: One of Europe's largest district heat operators; Berlin coal exit and heat-pump/waste-heat buildout underway.

companies.name: Fortum
companies.what: Nordic utility decarbonizing the ~2 TWh Espoo network — exited coal in 2025 and is integrating data-center heat, large heat pumps, electric boilers and storage.
companies.signal: Started operations at two heat-pump plants (180 MW district heat, 200 MW e-boilers, 800 MWh storage) for Microsoft data-center heat offtake, May 2026.

companies.name: E.ON
companies.what: Major district heating operator in Sweden and Germany and developer of ectogrid, a 5th-generation ambient loop that balances heating and cooling between buildings.
companies.signal: ectogrid running at Medicon Village in Lund and UK sites; among the European district heating market leaders.

companies.name: ENGIE
companies.what: Develops and operates district heating and cooling concessions worldwide, from Paris (CPCU) to the Gulf.
companies.signal: Consistently ranked among the top five global district heating players.

companies.name: Vicinity Energy
companies.what: Largest US district energy portfolio (Boston/Cambridge, Philadelphia and 10 other cities), electrifying legacy steam with 'eSteam' electric boilers and river-source heat pumps.
companies.signal: 42 MW electric boiler already producing carbon-free eSteam; broke ground Nov 2025 on a 35 MW Charles River heat pump complex with Everllence and DCO Energy, billed as the world's largest industrial-scale heat pump complex (complete ~2028).

companies.name: Danfoss
companies.what: Supplies district energy substations, valves, controls and the Leanheat AI software suite that lowers network temperatures and peak loads.
companies.signal: Named among district heating market leaders; Leanheat deployed across thousands of buildings and dozens of networks.

companies.name: Kamstrup
companies.what: Danish smart heat-meter and network-analytics maker whose ultrasonic meters enable low-temperature operation, billing and leak detection.
companies.signal: Standard metering kit for Nordic and German district heating; millions of heat meters shipped.

companies.name: Logstor (Kingspan)
companies.what: Market-leading maker of pre-insulated bonded pipe systems for district heating and cooling networks.
companies.signal: Acquired by Kingspan (2021); supplies major European network buildouts.

variations.name: District cooling providers & developers
variations.description: Central chiller plants and chilled-water loops serve dozens of buildings at roughly twice the efficiency of building-level air conditioning — critical infrastructure for hot-climate cities and increasingly financed like regulated utilities.

companies.name: Tabreed
companies.what: Gulf district cooling pioneer operating 90+ plants across the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Oman and India.
companies.signal: With CVC DIF completed the ~$1.03B acquisition of PAL Cooling (Oct 2025), adding eight Abu Dhabi concessions and 182,000 RT.

companies.name: Empower (Emirates Central Cooling Systems)
companies.what: World's largest district cooling provider by connected capacity, serving Dubai's major developments.
companies.signal: Q3 2025 revenue up 5.5%; targeting ~1.73-1.75M RT connected capacity by 2026; new 47,000 RT Dubai Science Park plant signed Aug 2025.

companies.name: PAL Cooling Holding
companies.what: Abu Dhabi district cooling operator with eight long-term concessions (182,000 RT connected).
companies.signal: Acquired by Tabreed and CVC DIF from Multiply Group for ~$1.03B, completed October 2025.

companies.name: Emicool
companies.what: Dubai district cooling utility expanding into solar-powered 'green cooling' districts.
companies.signal: Actis-backed; among the top Middle East district cooling providers.

companies.name: Keppel
companies.what: Operates Singapore's large underground district cooling systems (Marina Bay) and exports the model across Asia, including data-center-coupled cooling.
companies.signal: Marina Bay DCS is among the world's largest underground district cooling networks.

variations.name: Large-scale heat pumps & mechanical vapor recompression for district systems
variations.description: Multi-megawatt industrial heat pumps — often using natural refrigerants like CO2 and ammonia — lift heat from rivers, seawater, sewage, air or data centers to 70-150°C, replacing coal and gas CHP as the workhorse of district heat decarbonization.

companies.name: Everllence (formerly MAN Energy Solutions)
companies.what: Builds the world's largest CO2-refrigerant heat pumps for district heating, adapted from marine turbomachinery.
companies.signal: 70 MW seawater heat pump system in Esbjerg, Denmark ('biggest CO2 heat pump on the planet'); 33 MW Helsinki air-to-water unit ordered 2024 (world's largest, ~200 GWh/yr for 30,000 households); rebranded Everllence in 2025; supplying Boston's Vicinity complex.

companies.name: Siemens Energy
companies.what: Supplies large heat pumps delivering up to ~150°C for river-, sea- and waste-heat-source district heating.
companies.signal: 20 MWth Rhine river-source heat pump for MVV Mannheim delivering heat at 99°C for ~3,500 households (~10,000 t CO2/yr avoided).

companies.name: GEA Group
companies.what: German engineering group supplying ammonia heat pump systems for city-scale projects including mine-water and sewage-source schemes.
companies.signal: Heat pumps power Gateshead, the UK's largest mine-water heat network; Stadtwerke Lemgo wastewater-to-heat contract (2024).

companies.name: Star Refrigeration
companies.what: Glasgow-based independent ammonia heat pump pioneer behind Drammen, Norway's 90°C fjord-source district heating system.
companies.signal: Drammen 13+ MW system running since 2011; delivered Queens Quay Clydebank 5 MW river-source scheme in Scotland.

companies.name: Johnson Controls
companies.what: Supplies Sabroe-brand large natural-refrigerant heat pumps and chillers widely used in Scandinavian district energy plants.
companies.signal: Ranked among the top global large-scale natural-refrigerant heat pump suppliers.

companies.name: Friotherm
companies.what: Swiss maker of Unitop turbo heat pumps powering flagship plants such as Helsinki's Katri Vala sewage/seawater heat pump station.
companies.signal: Katri Vala is among the world's largest heat-pump heating/cooling plants (150+ MW heating).

variations.name: Data-center & industrial waste-heat reuse into buildings and networks
variations.description: Compute and industrial facilities reject enormous low-grade heat; capturing it via heat exchangers and heat pumps into district networks — or placing compute directly inside pools and buildings — turns a cooling cost into revenue and displaces gas, increasingly mandated by laws like Germany's Energy Efficiency Act.

companies.name: Stockholm Exergi
companies.what: Runs 'Open District Heating', a standing offer that pays data centers and supermarkets to feed recovered heat into Stockholm's network.
companies.signal: Recovers heat from dozens of data centers; the reference model for utility-side waste-heat offtake worldwide.

companies.name: Microsoft
companies.what: Supplying waste heat from its new Finnish data center region to Fortum's Espoo district network in the world's largest data-center heat-recovery deal.
companies.signal: Heat offtake to cover ~40% of the 2 TWh annual demand for 250,000 users; Fortum's recovery plants live May 2026, ~400,000 t CO2/yr avoided.

companies.name: Deep Green
companies.what: UK firm dropping immersion-cooled 'digital boiler' edge data centers into swimming pools, leisure centres and heat networks, giving the heat away free.
companies.signal: £200M investment from Octopus Energy (Jan 2024); first pool cut heating bills >60%; pipeline of 100-150 pools.

companies.name: Qarnot
companies.what: French 'computing heater' company whose QBx rack units deliver HPC waste heat directly into district heating networks.
companies.signal: Brescia deployment with utility A2A targeting 16 GWh/yr of heat for ~1,350 apartments; new European Innovation Council funding in 2025.

companies.name: Heata
companies.what: Centrica/British Gas-incubated startup that mounts cloud compute servers on domestic hot-water cylinders, giving households free hot water.
companies.signal: ~£1M seed round; hundreds of UK homes hosting units.

companies.name: Equinix
companies.what: Colocation giant offering formal heat-export programs from its data centers to nearby networks and facilities.
companies.signal: Its Saint-Denis data center heats the Paris 2024 Olympic Aquatics Centre; heat export offered across European IBX sites.

variations.name: Wastewater & sewage heat recovery
variations.description: Sewers carry 10-25°C water year-round; in-pipe or pumped heat exchangers plus heat pumps recover this heat for buildings and district loops — proven physics that remains under-deployed relative to the resource.

companies.name: SHARC Energy
companies.what: Vancouver-listed maker of SHARC and PIRANHA wastewater energy transfer systems for buildings, campuses and district energy plants.
companies.signal: Record 2025 revenue of $3.04M (+40% YoY) with $6.9M backlog; ~$4.6M new orders in early 2026 including Ottawa's LeBreton Flats district system and a Calgary treatment plant.

companies.name: Huber SE
companies.what: German wastewater-technology maker whose ThermWin system harvests heat from raw sewage via screened above-ground heat exchangers.
companies.signal: Dozens of ThermWin installations across Europe; referenced in US state technology assessments.

companies.name: Uhrig Energie
companies.what: German firm whose Therm-Liner modular heat exchangers retrofit directly into existing sewer pipes.
companies.signal: 60+ installations including municipal projects across DACH markets.

variations.white_space: Cheap, proven physics but fragmented adoption: every project needs sewer-utility access agreements and custom engineering, and category leader SHARC's ~$3M revenue after a decade shows how slow sales cycles are. The opening is standardized, code-driven products sold through heat-network developers and mandates (Vancouver-style low-carbon energy systems, Scandinavian and German waste-heat rules).

variations.name: Seasonal & underground thermal energy storage (ATES, BTES, pit, caverns, heat batteries)
variations.description: Storing summer heat or cheap wind/solar electricity as heat in aquifers, boreholes, water pits, rock caverns or sand silos lets networks shift renewable heat across days to seasons, cutting peak fossil boilers and power-market exposure.

companies.name: Polar Night Energy
companies.what: Finnish 'sand battery' pioneer storing 500°C+ heat in sand/crushed-rock silos charged with cheap electricity, discharged into district heating.
companies.signal: 1 MW/100 MWh Pornainen unit commissioned June 2025 (world's largest, cut local DH emissions ~60%); 250 MWh order from Lahti Energia announced Nov 2025.

companies.name: Vantaan Energia
companies.what: Finnish municipal utility building Varanto, the world's largest cavern thermal energy storage — 1.1M m³ of 140°C water in bedrock caverns.
companies.signal: 90 GWh capacity, ~€200M project with €19M state grant; excavation began 2024, completion ~2030.

companies.name: Aalborg CSP
companies.what: Danish integrated-energy EPC that owns the pit thermal energy storage (PTES) technology acquired from Arcon-Sunmark and delivers pit storage alongside solar district heating.
companies.signal: Acquired Arcon-Sunmark's PTES technology; active pit-storage and DH project pipeline in Denmark and Germany.

companies.name: IF Technology
companies.what: Dutch subsurface engineering firm behind much of the Netherlands' ~3,500-system aquifer thermal energy storage (ATES) fleet and its high-temperature ATES pilots.
companies.signal: NL operates ~3,500 ATES systems — the world's densest fleet; IF led HT-ATES state-of-the-art work in the EU HEATSTORE program.

companies.name: Kyoto Group
companies.what: Oslo-listed maker of the Heatcube molten-salt power-to-heat battery feeding district heating and industrial steam.
companies.signal: 4 MW/18 MWh Heatcube at Norbis Park district heating (Denmark); 56 MWh unit inaugurated at KALL Ingredients, Hungary (Oct 2025) — billed as the world's largest industrial TES; Iberdrola-backed.

companies.name: Hyme Energy
companies.what: Danish Seaborg spinout storing heat in molten hydroxide salts for district heat and industrial steam.
companies.signal: MOSS demonstration plant in Esbjerg supplying district heating since 2024; early commercial industrial contracts.

variations.name: Solar thermal district heating
variations.description: Hectare-scale flat-plate or concentrating collector fields feed 40-90°C water directly into district networks, often paired with pit storage — proven at gigawatt scale in Denmark but now a consolidating, policy-sensitive niche squeezed by cheap large heat pumps.

companies.name: Aalborg CSP
companies.what: Delivers turnkey solar-thermal district heating plants and hybrid integrated energy systems.
companies.signal: Recent orders include 4.7 MW for Stadtwerke Sondershausen (Germany) and an 8 MWth field for SK Forsyning (Denmark).

companies.name: Meriaura Energy (formerly Savosolar)
companies.what: Finnish maker of large MEGA flat-plate collectors for district heating and industrial heat; the chronically loss-making Savosolar business was restructured under Meriaura Group in June 2023.
companies.signal: Operating as Meriaura Energy since mid-2023; delivered some of Europe's largest collector fields (France, Denmark, Germany).

companies.name: Arcon-Sunmark
companies.what: Former world leader that built most of the world's large solar district heating fields from Denmark.
companies.signal: Wound down around 2020-21 as the Danish solar DH market stalled; its unique pit-storage (PTES) technology was sold to Aalborg CSP.

companies.name: GREENoneTEC
companies.what: Austrian operator of the world's largest flat-plate collector factory, supplying big district heating fields such as Graz.
companies.signal: Supplier behind record German and Austrian solar DH fields as that market hit new milestones.

companies.name: Heliac
companies.what: Danish maker of polymer Fresnel-lens collector fields producing district heat, aiming below flat-plate costs.
companies.signal: Two full-scale fields operating in Denmark (including ~1.2 MW Lendemarke); SDG Tech Awards finalist.

variations.white_space: The Danish home market stalled once utilities pivoted to large heat pumps and pit storage charged with cheap wind power — killing market leader Arcon-Sunmark and forcing Savosolar's restructuring. The remaining opening is hybrid plants (collectors + PTES + heat pumps) in Germany and Eastern Europe, where gas displacement economics and EU funds still favor solar heat.

variations.name: Geothermal direct-use district heating (deep geothermal & mine water)
variations.description: Wells tap hot aquifers, deep closed loops or flooded coal mines to feed 40-110°C heat straight into district networks — zero-fuel baseload heat now being industrialized by developers with oil-and-gas drilling skills.

companies.name: Innargi
companies.what: A.P. Moller Holding-backed developer that finances, drills and operates geothermal heat plants for district heating utilities under heat-as-a-service contracts.
companies.signal: EU's largest geothermal district heating project: first Aarhus plant online 31 Oct 2025 under a 30-year deal with utility Kredsløb; ~110 MW across three facilities by 2030; pipeline in Germany and Poland.

companies.name: Eavor Technologies
companies.what: Calgary firm whose closed-loop multilateral 'Eavor-Loop' wells produce heat (and power) without needing a hydrothermal aquifer, enabling geothermal heat almost anywhere.
companies.signal: Geretsried, Bavaria plant delivered first closed-loop grid power Dec 2025 with heat offtake to the local district network; backed by a €91.8M EU Innovation Fund grant and EIB financing.

companies.name: Stadtwerke München (SWM)
companies.what: Munich's city utility running Europe's most aggressive deep-geothermal district heating buildout (six plants including Schäftlarnstraße).
companies.signal: Targets climate-neutral district heating by 2040, anchored on Bavarian Molasse Basin geothermal.

companies.name: Gateshead Energy Company / Mining Remediation Authority
companies.what: Council-owned UK scheme pumping ~15°C flooded-mine water through GEA heat pumps into Gateshead's district network.
companies.signal: Live since March 2023; Britain's largest mine-water heat network, officially reviewed as a success and being expanded with new grant funding.

companies.name: Mijnwater
companies.what: Heerlen (NL) operator of Europe's flagship 5th-generation mine-water heating and cooling grid built on abandoned coal mines.
companies.signal: €13.5M EU Just Transition grant (June 2025) to expand the Zuid-Limburg grid; plans ~30,000 home connections by 2030; 100% renewable supply.

companies.name: CeraPhi Energy
companies.what: UK firm retrofitting closed-loop downhole heat exchangers (CeraPhiWell) into existing oil, gas and legacy wells for direct-use heat.
companies.signal: Demonstrator at a former UK fracking site; commercial traction beyond demos remains limited.

variations.name: District energy digitalization & optimization software
variations.description: AI and digital-twin platforms model entire heating grids in real time to cut supply temperatures, peak loads and CO2 by 5-20% without new hardware — typically the cheapest decarbonization lever available to network operators.

companies.name: Gradyent
companies.what: Rotterdam-based real-time digital twin for heating and cooling grids, used to run networks on 'autopilot' (Helen Helsinki, Vattenfall, Veolia Poland, Shell's Rotterdam steam grid, TU Delft).
companies.signal: €28M Series B (April 2025), total funding >€39M; claims up to 10% CO2 and 20% capex savings.

companies.name: Danfoss (Leanheat)
companies.what: Leanheat AI software suite (acquired Finnish startup, 2019) for thermo-hydraulic network modeling plus building-level demand control.
companies.signal: Deployed across thousands of buildings and major utilities as part of Danfoss's district energy portfolio.

companies.name: NODA Intelligent Systems
companies.what: Swedish AI platform for demand-side district heating optimization and data-center heat-reuse orchestration.
companies.signal: Two decades of deployments across Nordic and European networks; positioning in the data-center waste-heat boom.

companies.name: Utilifeed
companies.what: Gothenburg SaaS using digital twins and ML for district heating analytics, forecasting and customer-demand matching.
companies.signal: SEK 21M (~€1.9M) raised from Hafslund, Eidsiva and angels; pilots with 10 Swedish district heating companies and the Swedish Energy Agency.
